executiveSummary.scenarioTitle: Scenario A: Monsoon Downpour & Low-Lying Waterlogging
keyFindings: Ward L (Kurla / Sakinaka / Asalpha) holds the highest hazard score of 68 / 100 with an estimated 162 000 exposed residents (populationEst 900 000)
Citywide exposure is projected at 880 600 residents, yielding a mean susceptibility index of 47.7 / 100 and triggering an ORANGE_ALERT
Selected Ward F/South (Parel / Sewri / Naigaon) scores 58.5 / 100, has mean elevation 4.8 m, and 31 200 exposed residents; it contains three municipal hospitals including KEM Hospital
Simulation parameters applied: rainfall rate 45 mm/h, event duration 3 h, drainage blockage 15 % – these drive the computed scores

mainPotentiallyAffectedAssets.caveat: Located in spatial screening proximity (<500m); physical water ingress not confirmed.
Road centerline intersects modeled basin buffer; traffic impassability subject to spot depth.
Documented elevation minima where gravity storm-water discharge reverses during high tide.

criticalLimitations: Screening index (0-100) represents relative vulnerability, NOT calibrated 2D Saint-Venant flood depth.
Dam-break hydrodynamics and culvert breach events are not dynamically solved in Tier 2.
All population counts represent residential census totals within basin boundaries, not casualties.
immediateReviewPriorities: Pre-position high-capacity mobile dewatering pumps at Hindmata and Kurla depressions.
Activate traffic police standby for potential diversions at King Circle and Milan subway.
Liaise with KEM and Sion hospital maintenance teams for ground-floor sump power checks.

methodologyAndCalculation.formulaLatex: S_pond = min(100, 0.40 * (P * I - C * (1 - B)) + 0.25 * D_topo + 0.20 * H_hotspot + 0.15 * d_drainage)
methodologyAndCalculation.formulaPlain: S_pond = min(100, 0.40 * (P * I - C * (1 - B)) + 0.25 * D_topo + 0.20 * H_hotspot + 0.15 * d_drainage)

variableDefinitions.name: Precipitation / Hydraulic Forcing
variableDefinitions.normalizationMethod: Linear min-max normalization bounded at extreme monsoon rate (150 mm/h)
variableDefinitions.weightRationale: Primary volumetric driving force for urban pluvial accumulation.

variableDefinitions.name: Topographic Vulnerability (DEM Elevation)
variableDefinitions.normalizationMethod: Inverse elevation scaling from Copernicus GLO-30 (elevation < 6m = max score)
variableDefinitions.weightRationale: Gravity drainage terminates in saucer basins below mean high-tide level.

variableDefinitions.name: Chronic Hotspot Density
variableDefinitions.normalizationMethod: Logarithmic density scaling based on MCGM 35 official chronic locations
variableDefinitions.weightRationale: Empirical historical evidence of localized surface drainage bottlenecks.

variableDefinitions.name: Drainage Infrastructure / Blockage Constraint
variableDefinitions.normalizationMethod: Direct percentage of outfall constriction or pump deficit
variableDefinitions.weightRationale: Captures outfall tide-locking or solid-waste obstruction.

methodologyAndCalculation.baselineDefinition: Dry-weather baseline assuming 0 mm/h rain, 1.5m astronomical tide, 0% drainage blockage, and historical hotspot background. Delta percent represents: ((Score - Baseline) / max(1, Baseline)) * 100%.
methodologyAndCalculation.spatialResolution: 24 Canonical BMC Administrative Wards + 250m Continuous Raster Grid
methodologyAndCalculation.temporalResolution: Hourly increments from T+0h to T+6h
coreAssumptions: Rainfall intensity is distributed across ward polygons unless a continuous spatial grid is explicitly active.
Gravity runoff velocity is neglected; ponding is estimated on static topographic depressions.
Outfall sluice gates operate according to modeled scenario status without automated emergency override.
methodologyAndCalculation.validationStatus: Benchmarked against historical MCGM flooding records (2005, 2017, 2020) and Copernicus GLO-30 topographic minimums.

operationalThresholds.recommendedAdministrativePosture: Activate EOC incident desk; pre-deploy dewatering pumps; issue public traffic advisories.
Inspect low-lying underpasses; stand by ward quick response teams; check pump fuel.
Maintain routine telemetry monitoring; review roadside drain clearance reports.

stepByStepCalculations: Drainage Basin: Hindmata-Parel Central Low-Lying Bowl & Sewri Outfalls
Calculation Breakdown: Score = [RainExcess(9.0) + TopoSink(25) + Hotspots(25) + Drainage(11.5)] × TimeBuildup(0.83) = 58.5

citywideAssessment.populationExposureMethodology: Estimated based on 2011 Census projected to 2026, bounded by spatial intersection with documented low-lying depression sub-catchments (stepped exposure factor: 0% for Low, 5% for Moderate, 15% for High, 30% for Severe).
coverageGapsAndUncertainties: Underground stormwater pipe cross-sectional flow capacities are not modeled in real-time.
Informal settlement localized micro-drainage networks lack high-resolution GIS shapefiles.
Groundwater table saturation status is assumed uniform across coastal vs inland wards.

knownDataGaps: Real-time water depth telemetry via ultrasonic sensors is not available across all 35 hotspots.
Culvert siltation depth is based on pre-monsoon inspection logs, not continuous load cell monitoring.
Sluice gate status reflects simulated scenario constraints rather than real-time SCADA feedback.
scientificDisclaimers: TIER 2 EMPIRICAL SCREENING MODEL: The scores produced by this system represent dimensionless multi-criteria susceptibility indices (0-100). They are NOT numerical solutions of the 2D Shallow Water (Saint-Venant) equations and do NOT represent certified flood depths in meters.
NON-CALIBRATED FLOOD ENVELOPE: Spatial surfaces communicate relative gradient intensity across topographic basins. They must not be interpreted as physical dam-break inundation boundaries.

POPULATION EXPOSURE BOUNDING: Reported exposed population figures represent residents within low-lying sub-catchment screening buffers. They do NOT denote confirmed casualties, displaced families, or mandatory evacuation counts.
limitationsAndGovernance.administrativeDisclaimer: This Canonical Simulation Dossier is an automated decision-support artifact produced for municipal administrative review by MCGM emergency management officials. Recommendations and risk scores do NOT replace formal operational directives issued by the Municipal Commissioner, Additional Municipal Commissioners, or the Director of Disaster Management.
